summary:
The record shows a preexisting cervical condition that predates the motor vehicle accident at issue. On 2022-09-03, the patient sustained neck pain and stiffness during a weightlifting accident at the gym, reportedly occurring during a heavy squat set, per Dr. Alistair Finch at Back & Spine Restoration Center (the record notes a discrepancy regarding the exact date of this injury). An intake questionnaire was completed on 2022-09-10, and on 2022-09-12 Dr. Finch diagnosed acute cervical strain with possible underlying cervical disc herniation or bulge, also noting prior treatment for cervicalgia earlier in 2022. A three-view cervical spine X-ray on 2022-09-15 showed mild degenerative disc disease at C5-C6 with a 4mm posterior disc bulge — later characterized by Dr. Elizabeth Foster as of unclear onset/possibly preexisting, and by Dr. Myrtle Turner as a pre-existing 4mm posterior disc bulge at C5-C6 documented prior to the September 2023 incident.

The subject motor vehicle accident occurred with the patient presenting for emergency treatment; on 2023-09-04 Dr. Elizabeth Foster at Littel Inc Emergency Hospital arranged emergency consultation for open reduction and internal fixation of left arm fractures, with surgical procedures performed on the left arm that day using a nerve block tray for anesthesia. A CT scan of the head without contrast was performed 2023-09-05, and Acetaminophen 975mg was administered 2023-09-06 for pain. Fluoroscopic imaging was used intraoperatively on 2023-09-07 (Dr. Turner) to confirm hardware placement.

Post-surgical care began with physical therapy at Lang-Weimann Medical Center starting 2023-09-15 for left humerus/radius ORIF, cervicalgia, and left knee contusion, continuing through 2023-12-08 (30 sessions total, documented complete 2023-12-11) with cervical traction, soft tissue mobilization, and progressive extremity exercises; symptoms were repeatedly provoked. Surgical staples were removed 2023-09-21. Medications included Oxycodone-Acetaminophen 5-325mg (2023-09-22), Cyclobenzaprine 10mg starting 2023-10-19, and high-dose Ibuprofen 800mg starting 2023-11-16. X-rays on 2023-10-19 showed early callus; by 2023-12-14, imaging showed well-healed fractures with stable hardware, though MRI of the left upper extremity and C-spine was ordered for persistent restrictions and decreased radial sensation.

A significant gap occurred: the patient missed three consecutive PT sessions (2023-11-14, 11-17, 11-21), causing rebounded elbow stiffness noted 2023-11-24.

Care transitioned to Emory Sports Medicine Complex beginning 2024-01-08, continuing through discharge on 2024-03-22 (30 additional sessions), with repeated provoked cervical symptoms (1/17, 1/29, 2/12, 2/28, 3/4, 3/6). By 2024-02-08, Dr. Turner documented complete bony fusion with limited forearm/shoulder ROM. Final status on 2024-03-25 documented a persistent 15-degree extension deficit in the left elbow and chronic pain despite completed rehabilitation.
